title: Not Balanced
body:
Critical Strike has the potential to be a fun mobile shooter, but unfortunately the game is heavily built around spending money. Upgrading weapons takes an excessive amount of time and resources, making progression feel extremely slow unless you’re willing to pay. The cost to improve weapons or unlock better gear is simply too high compared to the rewards you earn from playing.

The reward system also feels very unbalanced. You can spend a lot of time completing matches, only to receive minimal rewards that barely help with upgrades. This creates a frustrating cycle where progress feels locked behind paywalls rather than skill or effort.

Overall, the gameplay itself can be enjoyable, but the economy of the game makes it hard to recommend. Unless the developers rebalance the upgrade costs and rewards, I wouldn’t suggest downloading it if you’re looking for a fair and rewarding experience.

title: Fun gameplay killed by greed
body:
Critical Strike has genuinely fun gameplay and can be addicting when matches are balanced. The gunplay feels smooth, the fast-paced action keeps you engaged, and there’s definitely potential for this game to be great. Unfortunately, all of that fun gets drowned out by how aggressively pay-to-win the game feels.

If you don’t spend money, progressing becomes frustratingly slow, and you’re basically forced to fight players with massively upgraded gear and stats. It’s discouraging loading into matches as a level 61 player only to get matched against level 100 players who completely dominate the lobby. There’s little sense of fair competition or balanced matchmaking, and skill often takes a backseat to whoever has spent the most money.

The game could be much better if developers focused on fair matchmaking and balanced progression instead of pushing players toward constant purchases.
